notes: Architecture ground truth — most subjective of the five. Focus on structural patterns: layering, dependency direction, boundary discipline, replaceability of side-effects. Lower thresholds than security/deps.

findings.summary: main.ts is a god-module: window lifecycle, simulator wiring, real-serial connection, OBD session state, 9 IPC handlers, Claude assistant routing, log export, CSV export, app lifecycle — all in one 400-line file with no internal seam.
findings.evidence: main.ts holds: createWindow, startSimulator, releaseActivePort, connectToPort, wireELMEvents, startOBDManager, 9 ipcMain.handle blocks, claude:ask controller management, app lifecycle hooks. All in a flat module with shared module-level lets.
findings.recommendation: Split into: main/window.ts (BrowserWindow + lifecycle), main/session.ts (an AppSession class owning elm/obd/simulator/port), main/ipc/obd.ts + main/ipc/claude.ts + main/ipc/session.ts (handler registration grouped by concern). main.ts becomes ~30 lines of composition.

findings.summary: No Transport abstraction between ELM327Commander and its two consumers (real SerialPort, simulator). The simulator branch is hand-wired with a FakeEmitter + setTimeout in startSimulator(), and the real branch is hand-wired with port.on('data')/port.write(). A third transport (USB-only adapter, network-bridged adapter, replay-from-log) requires copy-pasting either branch.
findings.evidence: startSimulator and connectToPort both construct an ELM327Commander(sendFn) by hand and route incoming bytes back via different shapes (EventEmitter vs port.on). No common Transport interface exists.
findings.recommendation: Define `interface ELMTransport { send(data: string): void; onData(cb: (chunk: string) => void): void; close(): Promise<void>; }`. SerialTransport and SimulatorTransport implement it. ELM327Commander accepts a Transport, not a sendFn + manual onData calls.

findings.summary: OBDProtocolManager embeds a DTC knowledge base (DTC_DB) — 39 hand-coded DTC descriptions, causes, repairs — inside the protocol layer. The protocol layer should know how to read codes from the bus; the knowledge of what they mean is a separate concern (and one likely to grow with each new vehicle platform).
findings.evidence: obdProtocolManager.ts:300–339 declares DTC_DB inline; getDTCDescription/Causes/Repair/Module look up from it. The PlatformProfile / GMT800 module nearby exists for exactly this kind of vehicle-specific data.
findings.recommendation: Move DTC_DB into files/src/core/dtcKnowledgeBase.ts (or per-platform under platforms/). Inject a DTCResolver into OBDProtocolManager. Generic SAE codes stay in core; platform-enhanced codes live in their platform module.

findings.summary: SessionContext crosses the renderer→main IPC boundary as a structurally-typed object with no validation. The main process trusts the renderer to send well-formed liveData/dtcs/recentLogs arrays — but it's also the only thing standing between malformed input and the Claude API.
findings.evidence: claudeAsk handler passes `context: SessionContext` straight through to formatContext, which interpolates fields directly into the prompt. No schema validation, no length cap, no shape check.
findings.recommendation: Add an IPC-boundary validator (zod or a hand-rolled `parseSessionContext(x: unknown): SessionContext`) that runs in the main process before askClaude is invoked. Reject malformed payloads with a typed error visible to the renderer.

findings.summary: ELM327Commander includes OBDLink-specific helpers (setSleepTimer via STSLLT, setPowerControl via STPC). The class is named for a generic ELM327 protocol but mixes vendor-proprietary AT-command extensions. The vendor split should be explicit (subclass, decorator, or capability-detection layer).
findings.evidence: elm327Commander.ts:222–230 — readBatteryVoltage uses generic ATRV (OK), but setSleepTimer / setPowerControl issue STSLLT / STPC which are OBDLink-only ScanTool extensions. Comments admit this.
findings.recommendation: Extract OBDLink-specific commands into `OBDLinkCommander extends ELM327Commander`, OR add a `capabilities` map populated during initialize() that gates vendor commands. Either way: the base class should not silently expose vendor methods.

findings.summary: PID_CATALOG is a top-level static array with closures over pure helpers; PID_MAP is a singleton Map keyed by PID. There's no way to inject an alternate catalog for tests (e.g. a subset for fast unit tests, or a platform-overridden catalog for vehicles with extended PIDs).
findings.evidence: export const PID_CATALOG: PIDDefinition[] = [...]; export const PID_MAP = new Map(PID_CATALOG.map(p => [p.pid, p])); — both are module-level constants. obdProtocolManager imports PID_MAP directly.
findings.recommendation: Replace direct PID_MAP imports with a `getPidMap()` accessor or pass the catalog into OBDProtocolManager via the constructor. Lets platforms (GMT800 et al.) extend the catalog without monkey-patching globals.

scoring.method: Architecture is the most subjective — thresholds matched to quality.
